# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From iteration cand_0001
- Give the proposer a first-class, sandboxed "dry-run a tool body against stubbed env_ primitives" affordance. I had to hand-roll an `exec`-with-injected-globals harness in /tmp to verify fire/no-fire and blast radius. This is the single highest-value verification step (it caught a dead fix: dropping a required `amount` field so the recoverable error path never triggered), yet nothing in the scaffold points you to it. A helper that loads `my_skill/scripts/<tool>.py`, injects named stubs, and runs given args would make VERIFY-THE-FIX cheap and standard rather than ad hoc.
- The failing-trace ARGS the model actually sent are the key input to verification, but they're buried in `.capevolve/run_suite/rollouts/<split>/` traces. A per-iteration `failing_args.json` (tool name → the exact arg dicts that errored, per failing task) would let the proposer verify against ground-truth inputs instead of reconstructing them from prose in the trajectory.
- Surface the reward_basis per task in the ranked-issue material. Task 11 had db_match=1.0 but reward=0.0 purely on the COMMUNICATE check — that distinction (DB-fix vs communicate-fix) changes the edit class entirely (enrich a return value vs change what gets persisted), and I only found it by reading traces closely.
